solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Particular kind of protection is celebrated by girls (10)

indicatorNotes.by: one piece sits by the next, so SUNG comes first and LASSES beside it

blocks.note: a deed celebrated in song is sung
lasses = girls

annotation.surface: Some special form of protection is being praised in song by a group of girls.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague: the particular protection is against the sun, which the first piece quietly supplies.
annotation.definitionFit: Sunglasses are a particular kind of protection, for the eyes against glare.

entries.clue: French author of Dune? (4)

blocks.note: the pen name of the 19th-century novelist Aurore Dupin
what a desert dune is made of

annotation.surface: A quiz question asking which French writer produced the novel Dune.
annotation.walkthrough: Dune is Frank Herbert's American novel, so no French author wrote it; the question mark warns that 'author of Dune' really means the stuff a dune is made from.
annotation.definitionFit: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin.

entries.clue: Family member‘s base within walls of Fort Knox, in complex (4,2,3)

indicatorNotes.within: the base goes within the walls
indicatorNotes.walls of: walls are the outside edges, so only F and T of FORT
indicatorNotes.complex: complex means intricately mixed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: e, the base of natural logarithms
outer letters of FORT, with E inside making FET
taken as it stands
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: A relative's base is somewhere inside the walls of Fort Knox, the heavily guarded US gold depository.
annotation.walkthrough: Base as e is the mathematical constant used as the base of natural logarithms. 'Fort Knox' wants to be read as a single place, but only Fort gives up its walls; Knox goes into the mix whole.
annotation.definitionFit: Your next of kin is your closest living relative, a family member.

entries.clue: Contents of typical Indian drink (5)

indicatorNotes.Contents of: contents are what's inside, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: typical = CLASSIC; its contents are everything but the outer Cs

annotation.surface: A description of what normally goes into an Indian drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contents of typical' looks like a hidden word in the letters of typical, but they do not hold it; typical must first become CLASSIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Lassi is a yoghurt-based drink from India.

entries.clue: Female figure repeatedly played western stereotype (7)

blocks.note: she = a female
a riff is a short musical figure played over and over

annotation.surface: A woman kept being cast in a stock role in westerns.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a shape or a number; in music it is a short phrase, and one repeated is a riff.
annotation.definitionFit: The sheriff is a stock figure of the western film.

entries.clue: Improve an empty castle after changes regularly rejected (7)

annotation.type: alternate letters + reversal + outer letters + charade

indicatorNotes.regularly: taking letters at regular intervals: cHaNgEs gives HNE
indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected means sent back, so HNE turns round
indicatorNotes.empty: an empty castle has nothing inside, leaving C and E
indicatorNotes.after: AN and CE come after the turned-round letters

blocks.note: alternate letters HNE of cHaNgEs, reversed
taken as it stands
CASTLE without its middle

annotation.surface: Advice to do up a derelict castle once alterations have been turned down.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a planning application for a ruin, with changes turned down; 'rejected' is really a reversal and 'regularly' picks every other letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to raise the quality or value of something.

entries.clue: Mark Carney, not backing foreign currency, backs dollar symbolically? (4)

indicatorNotes.not: not means without, so these letters go
indicatorNotes.backing: backing means written backwards: YEN becomes NEY
indicatorNotes.backs: CAR backs the S, standing behind it
indicatorNotes.symbolically: the dollar's symbol $ is an S with a stroke through it

blocks.note: the $ sign is a stroked S
CARNEY without NEY, the Japanese yen reversed

annotation.surface: Mark Carney, the Canadian former central banker, turns against foreign money and gets behind the dollar.
annotation.walkthrough: Mark Carney wants to be read as one name; Mark is the definition and only Carney is worked on. The yen is Japan's currency.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the lasting mark a healed wound leaves on skin.

entries.clue: Pet organisation based in Channel Islands (5)

indicatorNotes.based in: the organisation is based in, so placed inside, the islands

blocks.note: org. is the abbreviation for organisation
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, with ORG inside

annotation.surface: An animal charity with its headquarters on the Channel Islands, off the French coast.
annotation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British Crown dependencies near France, abbreviated CI.
annotation.definitionFit: A corgi is a breed of small dog, kept as a pet.

entries.clue: Poor team might face this concerning stage ahead of England, say, dismissing leader (10)

indicatorNotes.ahead of: LEG comes ahead of the next piece
indicatorNotes.dismissing leader: the leader is the first letter, so N goes

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in a letter heading
a leg is a stage of a journey or race
England is an example of a NATION; without its first letter, ATION

annotation.surface: A weak side might have to worry about a phase before playing England, with their captain sacked.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all sport, with a stage of a tournament and a dismissed captain, but the stage is a leg and 'say' marks England as one example of a nation. In British football the worst teams drop a division.
annotation.definitionFit: Relegation, dropping to a lower division, is what a poorly performing team faces.

entries.clue: Bond‘s almost succeeding with Felix Leiter’s homeland (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.with: the first piece is joined with the second

blocks.note: NEXT, as in succeeding, without its last letter
Felix Leiter is James Bond's CIA friend, so his homeland is the US

annotation.surface: James Bond nearly pulls off his mission alongside Felix Leiter, his American ally.
annotation.walkthrough: Bond wants to be James Bond, and Felix Leiter keeps the spy picture going, but Bond is the definition in its sense of a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connection or link between things, a bond.

entries.clue: Briefly, Harper Lee novel includes male fugitive (9)

indicatorNotes.Briefly: briefly means cut short, so HARPER loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.novel: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: HARPER cut short
taken as it stands
m = male

annotation.surface: In brief, a novel by Harper Lee, author of To Kill a Mockingbird, features a man on the run.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a noun to go with Harper Lee; here it is the adjective meaning new, the anagram signal. 'Fugitive' is the definition in its sense of fleeting, not a runaway.
annotation.definitionFit: Fugitive can mean fleeting or short-lived, which is what ephemeral means.

entries.clue: Admirer might be agitated to become this? (7)

annotation.definition: Admirer might be agitated to become this?

indicatorNotes.agitated: agitated means shaken up, so the letters are stirred

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A suitor might get nervous about the prospect of marriage.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: an admirer, shaken up, turns into someone married, and a nervous suitor might well end up that way.
annotation.definitionFit: An admirer's courtship may end with them married.

entries.clue: Take over wing (7)

blocks.note: o = over, the cricket abbreviation
a pinion is a bird's wing

annotation.walkthrough: 'Take over' reads as one phrase, to seize control; split it and Take is a noun, as in 'what's your take?'. In cricket, an over is a set of six balls.
annotation.definitionFit: Your take on something is your opinion of it.

entries.clue: Call to hold universal mourning (5)

indicatorNotes.to hold: RING holds the U inside it

blocks.note: to ring is to call on the phone
U = universal, the film certificate; it goes inside RING

annotation.surface: A summons for everyone to observe a period of grief.
annotation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: to rue is to regret bitterly, close to grieving over a loss.

entries.clue: Supplying core part of aqueduct with hose (10)

indicatorNotes.core part of: the core is the centre, the middle two letters of AQUEDUCT

blocks.note: stocking a shop is supplying it
middle letters of aquEDuct

annotation.surface: Delivering the central section of an aqueduct, complete with a hose.
annotation.walkthrough: Hose points to plumbing beside the aqueduct, but it is the old word for stockings or tights.
annotation.definitionFit: Stockinged means wearing stockings, that is with hose on.

entries.clue: Do launch (4-3)

blocks.note: an impression, as when a comic does a politician
an aircraft leaving the ground

annotation.walkthrough: Do reads as a party or as a plain verb, but it is the impressionist's do, as in 'he does a great Churchill'.
annotation.definitionFit: A take-off is both an impersonation, something one does, and an aircraft's launch.

entries.clue: Greek character alternatively keeping microphone on (7)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold on to it, so OR holds MIC within its letters

blocks.note: or = alternatively
mic is short for microphone; it goes inside OR
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: A figure from Greece, or perhaps a character in a Greek play, speaking with the mic switched on.
annotation.walkthrough: Character suggests a person, but here it is a letter of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Recipient of major prize in absence of nob, saving it for them? (7)

annotation.definition: Recipient of major prize in absence of nob, saving it for them?

indicatorNotes.in absence of: these letters are absent, so they come out
indicatorNotes.saving: the letters save, or keep, IT inside them

blocks.clueFragment: Recipient of major prize in absence of nob
blocks.note: a NOBELIST wins a Nobel prize; without NOB it is ELIST
taken as it stands; it goes inside ELIST, after EL

annotation.surface: A prizewinner whose award excludes the upper classes, but keeps it for them regardless.
annotation.walkthrough: A nob is an aristocrat or toff; an elitist wants things kept for the nobs, which is why the whole clue also defines the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An elitist would reserve things for the privileged, the 'them' of the clue.

entries.clue: Maybe taxed in April, late as ever (3,2,4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the words that follow

blocks.note: aprIL, LATE AS Ever

annotation.surface: Perhaps you paid tax in April and were as late with it as always.
annotation.walkthrough: Taxed looks like the tax return, with April the start of the British tax year, but it means strained or burdened.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone taxed, stretched or stressed, may be ill at ease.

entries.clue: Art caught on, but not initially (7)

indicatorNotes.but not initially: the initial letter is removed, so RUNNING loses its R

blocks.note: c = caught, the cricket abbreviation
a show that is on is RUNNING; without its first letter, UNNING

annotation.surface: A style of art became popular, though not at the start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught on' reads as one phrase meaning became popular; split, caught is C, as on a cricket scorecard, and on is running.
annotation.definitionFit: Art in its old sense of craft or guile is cunning.

entries.clue: Giant boar eating dog up (7)

indicatorNotes.eating: HOG eats TAIL, taking it inside
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read bottom to top

blocks.note: a hog is a boar
to dog someone is to tail them; inside HOG it makes HTAILOG, then read upwards

annotation.surface: A huge wild pig gobbles up a dog.
annotation.walkthrough: Dog looks like the animal, a natural meal for a boar, but it is the verb meaning to follow.
annotation.definitionFit: Goliath was the biblical giant slain by David.

entries.clue: Aim to cycle past masked Spaniard (7)

indicatorNotes.to cycle: the letters rotate: the G of GOAL moves round to the end
indicatorNotes.past: ALGO goes past, so after, HID

blocks.note: something masked is hid, an old past participle of hide
GOAL with its first letter moved to the end

annotation.surface: A plan to bike by a Spaniard in a mask.
annotation.walkthrough: Cycle suggests a bike ride; here it means rotate the letters of GOAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish gentleman of the lower nobility.

entries.clue: Increasingly difficult to stash nothing – for one? (7)

annotation.definition: Increasingly difficult to stash nothing – for one?

indicatorNotes.to stash: HARDER stashes, or hides, the O inside it

blocks.note: harder = more difficult
O looks like zero, nothing; it goes inside HARDER after H

annotation.surface: It keeps getting harder to put nothing away.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: for a hoarder, stashing nothing is always getting harder.
annotation.definitionFit: A hoarder is someone who finds it ever harder not to stash things away.

entries.clue: Gather in fruit, except raspberries at first (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of each word it covers

blocks.note: taken as it stands
first letters of Fruit, Except, Raspberries

annotation.surface: Harvest every fruit apart from the raspberries, which come first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gather in' reads as harvest, but in belongs to the wordplay; except looks like a deletion signal and only lends its E.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the reasoning sense, as in 'I gather you're leaving': to conclude from evidence.

entries.clue: Quick reconstruction of 24 avoiding parts of LA (5)

indicatorNotes.reconstruction of: the remaining letters are rebuilt in a new order
indicatorNotes.avoiding: the L and A are avoided, so left out

blocks.note: 24 across is LEAFLET; without one L and the A, EFLET

annotation.surface: A hasty rebuild of the 24 freeway, skirting parts of Los Angeles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts of LA' reads as districts of the city; here it means the letters L and A.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary adjective for swift, familiar from the phrase 'of foot'.

entries.clue: Tract of open land left out (7)

indicatorNotes.out: out means disordered, so LEFT is rearranged

blocks.note: a lea is open grassland
LEFT rearranged

annotation.surface: A stretch of open country has been excluded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tract of open land' reads as one phrase, but tract is the definition in its sense of a pamphlet.
annotation.definitionFit: A tract in its religious or political sense is a short printed pamphlet handed out to spread a message.

entries.clue: Stretch around side of bar, in this activity? (5)

annotation.definition: Stretch around side of bar, in this activity?

indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so LIMO wraps itself round the B
indicatorNotes.side of: one side, here the first letter, of BAR

blocks.note: a stretch is a stretch limo
first letter of BAR; it goes inside LIMO

annotation.surface: Bending your body around the edge of a bar is what this activity asks of you.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the dance: in limbo you stretch backwards under a bar.
annotation.definitionFit: Limbo is the dance in which you lean back to pass under a low bar.

entries.clue: Name taken by Busta Rhymes (4)

indicatorNotes.taken by: the answer is taken, held, by the words that follow

blocks.note: buSTA Rhymes

annotation.surface: A stage name chosen by the American rapper Busta Rhymes.
annotation.walkthrough: Name is the definition in its sense of a celebrity, as in 'a big name', which the rapper happens to be.
annotation.definitionFit: A name, meaning a famous person, is a star.

entries.clue: Covetousness to acquire northern network, here? (9)

annotation.definition: Covetousness to acquire northern network, here?

indicatorNotes.to acquire: GREED acquires the letters, taking them inside

blocks.note: greed = covetousness; it holds the rest after GREE
n = northern
LAN is a local area network

annotation.surface: A wish to take over a northern territory with its communications network.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Greenland is the northern territory that US president Donald Trump has openly coveted, which the question mark nods to.
annotation.definitionFit: The &lit reads straight: the Arctic island's strategic position and minerals have made it the target of open American designs.

entries.clue: Prime soldier possibly designed (5)

blocks.note: Prime is the setter's pseudonym, so Prime = ME
a soldier is one kind of ant

annotation.surface: A first-rate soldier, perhaps one designed that way.
annotation.walkthrough: Prime reads as first-rate, but it is this puzzle's setter naming himself, the usual 'me' device. Possibly flags soldier as an example: a soldier ant.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of intended, as in 'designed to fail'.

entries.clue: What naturally comes with Stone Age? (4)

blocks.note: a palm fruit that grows around a stone
a period of time, as in 'of recent vintage'

annotation.surface: A question about what naturally goes with the Stone Age.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stone Age' reads as one prehistoric period; split it, and a date comes with a stone and is also an age.
annotation.definitionFit: The date fruit grows with a stone, and date also means a time or age.

entries.clue: American rising in acclaim for Ben-Hur? (10)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so A and RIOT are placed inside CHEER

blocks.note: a = American
a rising is an uprising, a riot
a cheer is acclaim; A and RIOT go inside after CH

annotation.surface: An American actor receiving applause for his role in the film Ben-Hur.
annotation.walkthrough: Rising looks like a reversal signal but is a noun, a revolt. Ben-Hur is the hero of the novel and film famous for its chariot race; the question mark marks him as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Judah Ben-Hur is a charioteer, racing in the Roman circus.
